checks: Compact support and continuity give finite integrals and conditional Jensen applies where the martingale row barycenter exists. The nonnegative row gap has integral zero.

For each fixed row with zero gap, every supporting affine function gives a nonnegative target gap whose mean is zero by the same row barycenter identity. No slope needs to be selected measurably, and the source full-measure set was chosen before any slope.

For a fixed row, the closed affine contact set for every slope contains the support of the conditional law. This also explains simultaneous concentration if read as intersection over slopes. A countable intersection of the corresponding source sets preserves full measure.

For strictly convex Φ any supporting plane can meet its graph at only one point, so every zero-gap row is diagonal. For nonnegative Φ, starting at a zero and having zero gap forces the target law to stay in the zero set.

overlap.comparison: For Φ equal to the negative of a finite minimum of affine forms, the result gives concentration in all active contact cells and a separate dissipation identity. The frozen result covers every finite continuous convex Φ, all supporting slopes, and countable families.
Identifies zero Jensen defects for the specific finite concave centroid roof under the physical fixed-normal martingale. It does not quantify over arbitrary continuous convex equality tests.

readability: The contact sets are closed, so the row support formulation makes the simultaneous quantifier over possibly uncountably many slopes immediate.
review_method: Independent cold reading of the frozen proof, then direct checks of the archived source locators, pinned predecessors and mathematical arguments.
summary: Equality of the integrals forces zero conditional Jensen gap on one full-measure set. The asserted all-slope and countable-test quantifiers follow on that set.
